newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian parliament delays decision on budget cuts.
newsitem.headline: Russian parliament delays decision on budget cuts.

text.p: Russia's lower house of parliament on Wednesday rejected a plan to fill a budget revenue gap by doubling money supply and looked set to send government spending cut proposals to a special commission.

Deputies accepted in principle a suggestion that they look into exactly where the cuts would fall. They were due to vote again on the proposal later in the afternoon, but cannot change it substantially.
It includes creating a commission from representatives of the two houses of parliament and the government with the task of presenting proposals by June 18.

The chamber earlier rejected a proposal to alter the 1997 budget law to give the government sole responsibility for any cuts and also threw out a communist-inspired proposal to add 330 trillion roubles to money supply.
Revenues so far this year have been well below budgeted levels, forcing the government to make proposals on spending cuts under the 1997 budget.
